I'm older than most folks around here. When I was growing up, the size you were when you graduated high school was your size. You stopped growing around the end of high school; whatever size you were when you graduated was the one you were expected to be for the rest of your life. If you gained any weight during adulthood, you were expected to diet until you got back down to the size you were at the end of high school.

All of this is to say you stopped growing once you hit adulthood.

Nowadays, people keep getting bigger and bigger (read: fatter and fatter) and aren't ashamed of it! This is so weird to me. I grew up in a generation where it was expected that you stopped growing--that your body stopped changing--in early adulthood. The size you were at age 19 was the size you were going to be for the rest of your life (plus or minus 5-10 pounds...but even then, you were not allowed to be content with an extra 10 pounds on your body).
